item.text: {"text":"Dense `TransformerEncoder` attention preserves sequence slots: `src_key_padding_mask` excludes specified keys without deleting or renumbering tokens. Thus internal PAD holes retain their indices, and absolute positional embeddings added beforehand remain attached to those indices. Masking keys does not guarantee zero outputs at padded query positions; exclude those outputs from loss/readout. Nested conversion needs care: PyTorch’s source checks that valid tokens are left-aligned (padding forms a suffix), so left-padded histories or internal holes normally prevent automatic conversion with `mask_check=True`. Disabling that check bypasses this safeguard. For predictable slot preservation, use `enable_nested_tensor=False`; verify behavior against the installed version. These conclusions follow from the [official encoder implementation](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/v2.5.1/torch/nn/modules/transformer.py), not a local execution of the supplied model.\n\nBoolean mask polarity differs between APIs. In `MultiheadAttention`, `True` in `key_padding_mask` means ignore that key; `True` in its attention mask means block that attention connection. In functional `scaled_dot_product_attention`, `True` means allow attention. For direct SDPA with tensors shaped `[B,H,L,D]`, a PAD mask `[B,L]` therefore becomes `(~pad_mask)[:,None,None,:]` for key masking. Float masks instead add to attention logits, typically using zero for allowed entries and negative infinity for blocked entries. SDPA also requires explicitly setting `dropout_p=0.0` during evaluation. Check internal holes, left padding, and appended-mask readout in training and evaluation modes; gather the final nonpadding index, never `count-1`. Sources: [MultiheadAttention documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.modules.activation.MultiheadAttention.html), [SDPA documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention)."}
